decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75% to 4%. The vote was 10-2. Dissenting: Lisa D. Cook, Beth M. Hammack.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote:
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 12 – 0 vote:”

changes.quote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's du…”

changes.quote: Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace.”

changes.quote: The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Today's policy action will support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal.”

changes.quote: Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee will deliver price stability.
Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 20.94% APR costs about $87.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.05% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.4% would rise by about $12.29 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.2%, and employers added an average of 51k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4% over the past year (September 2026); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.28%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.15% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 69%, cut 2%, hike 29%.
